description: A web developer who lives on a farm and a university worker walked into a Met office building and looked to help farmers to improve their farm output with some suggestions that they may not have thought of.
summary:
This is a php app that takes NASA earth observation data and farmer inputted local data to create suggestions on crops to plant for the coming year and any extra inputs that might be needed such as water or things to change soil pH. Our longer term aim would be to including visual maps and crop rotation suggestions. Our app has code ready for these features by time was against us.

Farmers need to maintain the soil they work to maximize yield or at least bring in enough to keep going. Short term gains may lead to long term disaster. Crop rotation is a time honored practice of nutrient cycling that has been used for hundreds of years. Farmers balance many factors to decide what to plant next year; what will be in demand, how to prepare and how to treat it. Climate change means old routines of farm crop rotation may no longer be the best and new suggestions may be needed. Our app aims to help by making suggestions. The aim is not to give numbers, but to make actionable suggestions. Of course the farmer will make the final choices.
details:
The app as it stands allows a farmer to create an account, enter map co-ordinates, add pH readings they have taken already, plus the current crop and the soil type.

We then use the map co-ordinates to draw down NASA monthly average temperature, perception and root level wetness data.

By combining all this we can display information about some common crops grown in crop rotations and use that to give advice as to whether this crop would do well on the given site.

We used widely available data about crop rotation, crop patterns and crop requirements for pH, water requirements, soil types and temperature requirements. This is held in a database linked to the app.

In this prototype it does not actually take into account temperature just due to time pressure, however soil type and perception do combine with the NASA data to give suggestions.

Specific NASA data we used

  • GWEROOT (Root zone soil wetness)
  • (TSURF) Surface Temperature of Land and Snow
  • (PRECTORCORR) Precipitation Corrected

The skeleton php app was setup to allow us to bring in NASA and any other data that was required. The app includes some features we have not use at this point. There is the possibility to bring in a map function and also the ability to give suggestions on a possible full crop rotation scheme.

php app code is on github- https://github.com/helenc77/nasa-field-shift

Languages

PHP 53.9% JavaScript 38.6% CSS 6.1% Shell 1.4%

There is Docker being used and MariaDB.

the demo is published to https://www.clerkenwater.com which was some webspace we had available.

A user can create an account (email and password)

They then create a farm profiles by manually inputting:

  • Farm name
  • Location
  • Soil pH
  • current crop
  • Soil type

Then we compared this with information held in a database collected from farming websites and Google about crop types and their preferred soil conditions and rain fall requirements.

web resources

  • farmersadvisory.com
  • farmingweekly.com
  • thefarmingforum.co.uk

This comparison leads to data about a range of crops and their suitability. In the final app it would highlight which ones would be better in a crop rotation and give an idea of the order that might work well.

We used some personal experience of living on a farm to help guide what a farmer might need.

Our app is not fully featured enough to be of real use at this point, but does demonstrate potential. To be truly useful it would need additional relevant data such as elevation, temperature and using the soil type information which we have not used while building this prototype. Also long term weather, potential climate change issues, likely consumer demand and even diesel prices would be great, if we could achieve it!
